title: An Unusual Bilateral Presentation of Meigs' Syndrome in a Postmenopausal Woman: A Case Report.
abstract: Abstract Meigs' syndrome is a rare benign condition characterized by the triad of an ovarian tumor, ascites, and pleural effusion, often mimicking advanced ovarian malignancy. We report the case of a nulliparous woman in her late seventies who presented with a four-month history of progressive dyspnea, abdominal pain, and urinary frequency. Imaging revealed large bilateral solid adnexal masses measuring 17 cm and 15 cm, with no ascites detected initially. Tumor markers, including CA-125 (14 U/mL), were within normal limits. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated well-defined, non-enhancing solid masses without diffusion restriction, suggestive of benign ovarian stromal tumors. The Risk of Malignancy Index was 126, indicating low malignant potential. The patient underwent total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Intraoperatively, two distinct ovarian tumors measuring approximately 8 cm each were identified, along with 300 mL of clear ascitic fluid, representing interval development not detected on prior imaging. Histopathological examination confirmed bilateral ovarian fibromas. Cytology of ascitic fluid was negative for malignancy. Postoperatively, ascites and pleural effusions resolved completely, confirming the diagnosis of bilateral Meigs' syndrome. At follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic with no evidence of recurrence. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing Meigs' syndrome from ovarian malignancy, particularly in the presence of large bilateral masses. Integration of imaging characteristics, tumor markers, and risk stratification tools is essential to guide appropriate management and avoid unnecessary aggressive treatment.

title: Correlation of conventional histopathology and GeneXpert MTB/RIF in the diagnosis of spinal tuberculosis.
abstract: Introduction Spinal tuberculosis (STB) remains a significant health burden in tuberculosis-endemic regions, including India. Diagnosis is challenging because conventional microbiological methods, including acid-fast staining and mycobacterial culture, have limited sensitivity in paucibacillary disease. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of GeneXpert MTB/RIF in comparison with conventional histopathological examination (HPE) for the diagnosis of STB. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 64 patients with clinical and radiological suspicion of spinal tuberculosis who underwent transpedicular biopsy. Patients with definitive GeneXpert MTB/RIF and histopathological examination results were included. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 24.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Results Histopathology was positive in 46 (71.9%) patients, while GeneXpert MTB/RIF was positive in 63 (98.4%); both tests were positive in 45 (70.3%) cases. Compared with histopathology, GeneXpert demonstrated 97.83% sensitivity, 0% specificity, 71.43% positive predictive value, and 70.31% overall accuracy. The association between GeneXpert and HPE results was not statistically significant (χ² = 0.398, p = 0.528). Conclusion GeneXpert MTB/RIF is a rapid and sensitive adjunct to histopathology in the diagnosis of STB. However, the absence of specificity and the modest overall diagnostic accuracy observed in this study should warrant a cautious interpretation of this diagnostic tool.

title: Qualitative MRI Features for Differentiating GBM, Solitary Brain Metastasis, and Primary CNS Lymphoma: A Retrospective Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
abstract: Background Glioblastoma (GBM), solitary brain metastasis (SM), and primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) are important malignant brain tumors that may exhibit overlapping imaging features, making preoperative differentiation challenging. Although conventional MRI (cMRI) is widely available and routinely used in clinical practice, comprehensive comparative evaluation of cMRI features for differentiating these three entities remains limited. Purpose This study aimed to identify conventional MRI features distinguishing GBM, SM, and PCNSL, and to develop a diagnostic algorithm for initial evaluation. Material and methods This retrospective study included 108 patients (59 GBM, 24 SM, 25 PCNSL) who underwent pre-operative 3T brain MRI between May 2021 and May 2025, with histopathologic confirmation. The imaging features were compared using appropriate statistical tests. Statistically significant qualitative variables were then entered into a classification model built with the CHAID (Chi-square Automatic Interaction Detection) growing method. Results Significant differences were observed across tumor types in lesion location, border characteristics, enhancement patterns, and specific signs such as the notch sign, worm-like sign, and intra-tumoral vascular enhancement (all p < 0.05). PCNSLs commonly showed homogeneous enhancement and regular margins, while GBM and SM demonstrated heterogeneous ring enhancement, necrosis, and hemorrhage. The CHAID decision tree achieved an overall accuracy of 80.6%, with class-specific accuracies of 83.3% for GBM, 86.1% for SM, and 91.7% for PCNSL. Conclusions The proposed decision tree offers a practical tool for diagnostic orientation and treatment planning, particularly in settings without access to advanced imaging techniques.

title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease phenotypes and 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: Background The prognostic significance of lean metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease remains uncertain. We evaluated 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in lean versus non-lean MAFLD. Methods This prospective observational cohort study included 193 adults with MAFLD and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-defined obstructive coronary artery disease at Thong Nhat Hospital, Vietnam. Lean MAFLD was defined as a body mass index <23 kg/m² and non-lean MAFLD as a body mass index ≥23 kg/m². The primary outcome was the first expanded major adverse cardiovascular event (eMACE) within 365 days, including ischemia-driven coronary revascularization. Planned first percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) after baseline CCTA was included. Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Results During follow-up, 115 patients (59.6%) experienced eMACE. The eMACE rate was higher in lean than in non-lean MAFLD (86.2% vs 54.9%, P=0.002). Among these cases, recorded components were revascularization (108), myocardial infarction (13), unstable angina (26), acute heart failure (1), stroke (0), and cardiovascular death (0); components overlapped. These counts do not establish first-event attribution. Lean MAFLD remained associated with eMACE after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary artery disease (adjusted HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.32-3.26, P=0.002). Conclusions Among patients with MAFLD and obstructive coronary artery disease, lean MAFLD was associated with a higher 1-year hazard of eMACE than non-lean MAFLD, after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary disease. The small lean group and inclusion of planned revascularization limit extrapolation to non-revascularization events, confirmation in larger cohorts is needed.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Background Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously. Objectives To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Results Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry. Conclusions Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

title: [X-ray-guided lung puncture navigation integrating direct linear transformation-Gauss-Newton method and marker-free registration].
abstract: Percutaneous transthoracic needle biopsy (PTNB) is an important modality for the qualitative diagnosis of lung cancer, which relies on medical-image guidance. X-ray equipment features wide availability and low radiation dose; nevertheless, X-ray-guided PTNB requires repeated calibration using physical calibrators. Accordingly, this paper proposes an X-ray-guided lung puncture navigation method integrating the direct linear transformation-Gauss-Newton method (DLT-GNM) and marker-free registration. Preoperatively, initial imaging parameters are acquired via fluoroscopic calibration. Intraoperatively, a binocular camera tracks the spatial pose of the C-arm in real time to virtually reconstruct calibration points. DLT-GNM is employed to solve the projection model and realize marker-free real-time navigation. Respiratory phantom experiments show that the overall localization error is (0.38 ± 0.25) mm under matched respiratory phases. It is verified that this method delivers high accuracy and simple operation, and possesses favorable clinical application potential for cases with large lesions or identifiable targets clearly visualized under X-ray fluoroscopy.

title: [Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with double-bundle artificial ligament based on four-dimensional impingement free mechanism: a comparative study with single-bundle reconstruction].
abstract: Objective To investigate the surgical method of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction with double-bundle artificial ligaments based on four-dimensional impingement free mechanism, and to compare its short-term effectiveness with traditional single-bundle reconstruction. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 45 patients with complete ACL rupture who met the selection criteria and were treated between October 2022 and October 2025. Based on anatomical measurement results and surgical technique selection, patients were divided into a single-bundle reconstruction group (29 cases, receiving traditional over-the-top isometric single-bundle reconstruction) and a double-bundle reconstruction group [16 cases, receiving four-dimensional impingement free ACL double-bundle reconstruction (over-the-top anteromedial bundle+low posterolateral bundle)]. Baseline data-including age, injured side, cause of injury, concomitant meniscus injury, and preoperative Lysholm score, International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) score, and Tegner score-showed no significant difference between the two groups ( P >0.05); however, the difference in gender distribution between the two groups was significant ( P <0.05). Operation time, complications, knee range of motion, and the results of the Lachman test, anterior drawer test, and pivot-shift test were recorded. Knee function was evaluated using the Lysholm, IKDC, and Tegner scores preoperatively and at last follow-up, and the proportion of patients returning to pre-injury sports activity levels was calculated. Postoperative three-dimensional CT was performed to evaluate bone tunnel placement and graft-to-tunnel congruence. Results Operations were successfully completed in both groups, with the operation time in the double-bundle reconstruction group being significantly longer than that in the single-bundle reconstruction group ( P <0.05). All patients were followed up 6-13 months, with an average of 8.5 months. Patients in both groups resumed immediate postoperative knee range of motion reached 0°-135°, and normal independent walking at 2 weeks postoperatively. At last follow-up, the Lachman test and anterior drawer test were negative in all patients; the pivot-shift test was negative in all cases in the double-bundle reconstruction group, whereas 3 cases (all grade Ⅰ) were positive in the single-bundle reconstruction group, with no significant difference in the positive rate of the pivot-shift test between the two groups ( P >0.05). At last follow-up, the proportion of patients returning to pre-injury sports activity levels was significantly higher in the double-bundle reconstruction group than in the single-bundle reconstruction group ( P <0.05). Both the IKDC and Tegner scores showed significant improvement compared with preoperative values in the two groups ( P <0.05), while the Lysholm scores showed no significant difference when compared with preoperative values ( P >0.05). There was no significant difference in the pre- to post-operative change values of each score between the two groups ( P >0.05). Postoperative three-dimensional CT demonstrated that the distance between the margins of the anterior and posterior bone tunnels in the double-bundle reconstruction group was more than 5 mm, with no evidence of tunnel fracture or posterior cruciate ligament impingement; MRI showed favorable graft morphology without signs of impingement. During the follow-up, no severe complications such as graft laxity, rupture, or synovitis occurred in either group. Conclusion Under the guarantee of strict anatomical screening, artificial ligament double-bundle reconstruction based on four-dimensional impingement free mechanism shows a favorable clinical trend in restoring rotational stability, with pivot-shift control superior to that of single-bundle reconstruction. Combined with a higher rate of return to sports, it holds significant clinical value for athletic populations seeking early, high-quality rehabilitation. However, strict indication screening based on individualized anatomical conditions is essential for this surgical procedure.

title: [Effectiveness comparison of one-hole split endoscopy and unilateral biportal endoscopy discectomy via the superior articular process approach for L 5 , S 1 far lateral lumbar disc herniation].
abstract: Objective To compare the effectiveness between one-hole split endoscopy(OSE) and unilateral biportal endoscopy (UBE) discectomy via the superior articular process approach for L 5 , S 1 far lateral lumbar disc herniation (FLLDH). Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of 98 patients with L 5 , S 1 FLLDH who met the selection criteria and were admitted between January 2021 and December 2024. The patients were divided into an OSE group (52 cases) and a UBE group (46 cases) according to the surgical procedure. There was no significant difference in baseline data between the two groups ( P >0.05), such as age, gender, side, body mass index, preoperative anterior-posterior translation distance (ATD), disc height (DH), lumbar lordosis angle (LLA), visual analogue scale (VAS) scores for low back pain and leg pain, and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Operation time, intraoperative blood loss, intraoperative fluoroscopy frequency, incision length, and postoperative hospital stay were recorded. title: [Comparative study on effectiveness of two fixation methods in treatment of mid-column plantar-flexion Lisfranc injuries].
abstract: Objective To compare the effectiveness of open reduction with screw internal fixation versus primary arthrodesis for mid-column plantar-flexion Lisfranc injuries. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 45 patients (45 feet) with mid-column plantar-flexion Lisfranc injuries, who met the selective criteria between June 2019 and June 2022. Among them, 23 patients were treated with primary tarsometatarsal arthrodesis (arthrodesis group), and 22 patients received open reduction with screw internal fixation (screw group). There was no significant difference between groups ( P >0.05) in age, gender, body mass index, injured side, interval from injury to operation, Myerson classification, and preoperative visual analogue scale (VAS) score, American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) score, 36-Item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-36) score, the distance between the medial cuneiform and the second metatarsal (C1-M2), the distance between first and second metatarsal (M1-M2), step-off sign (SOS) displacement, and talus-first metatarsal angle (Meary angle). Operation time, incision length, intraoperative fluoroscopy frequency, intraoperative blood loss, time to initial weight-bearing, time to full weight-bearing, and postoperative complications during follow-up were recorded and compared. Pain and functional recovery were evaluated using VAS, AOFAS, and SF-36 scores. Radiographic parameters including C1-M2, M1-M2, SOS displacement, and Meary angle were measured during follow-up. Intergroup differences in the changes of the all outcome indicators from preoperative to last follow-up were also compared. Results All patients underwent successful operation. The arthrodesis group had significantly longer operation time, longer incision length, more intraoperative fluoroscopy exposures, and greater intraoperative blood loss compared with the screw group ( P <0.05). All patients were followed up 24-36 months (mean, 27.6 months). No significant intergroup difference was found in time to initial weight-bearing or time to full weight-bearing ( P >0.05). At last follow-up, the indicators for function, pain, and imaging in both groups significantly improved compared with those before operation ( P <0.05). The arthrodesis group achieved significantly greater changes of AOFAS score, VAS score, SF-36 score, and Meary angle than the screw group ( P <0.05). No significant intergroup difference was found in the changes of C1-M2, M1-M2, and SOS ( P >0.05). The incidence of complication was significantly lower in arthrodesis group (8.6%, 2/23) than in screw group (36.3%, 8/22) ( P <0.05). Conclusion For mid-column plantar-flexion Lisfranc injuries, primary tarsometatarsal arthrodesis yields better functional recovery and pain relief compared with open reduction and screw internal fixation.

title: [Effectiveness of arthroscopic grid-pattern dynamic rotator cuff reconstruction using autologous tendon graft for irreparable massive rotator cuff tears].
abstract: Objective To evaluate effectiveness of arthroscopic grid-pattern dynamic rotator cuff reconstruction using autologous tendon graft in treatment of irreparable massive rotator cuff tears (IMRCT). Methods A retrospective case series study was conducted on 32 patients with IMRCT treated between July 2022 and December 2023. All patients underwent arthroscopic grid-pattern dynamic rotator cuff reconstruction using autologous peroneus longus tendon graft. There were 11 males and 21 females, aged 49-76 years (mean, 65 years). The clinical symptoms were joint pain accompanied by limited mobility and abduction weakness. The duration of preoperative symptoms ranged from 3 to 24 months (mean, 9 months). Pain was assessed using the visual analogue scale (VAS) score, and shoulder function was evaluated using the modified University of California at Los Angeles (UCLA) score and the Constant-Murley score before operation and at 3, 6, 12 months after operation. MRI was performed during follow-up to assess graft integrity. Complications were recorded. Results The operation time ranged from 75 to 130 minutes, with a mean of 90 minutes. All incisions healed by first intention, and no significant complication or adverse reaction was observed. All patients were followed up 12-24 months (mean, 16.5 months). All postoperative scores improved significantly when compared with preoperative values ( P <0.05). Pain and function continued to improve over time; no significant difference was observed in the modified UCLA scores among 6 months, 12 months, and last follow-up, nor in any scores between 12 months and last follow-up ( P >0.05); all other pairwise comparisons showed significant differences ( P <0.05). At last follow-up, shoulder function was rated as excellent in 12 cases, good in 18 cases, and poor in 2 cases according to the modified UCLA scoring system, yielding an excellent-to-good rate of 93.8%. MRI follow-up demonstrated intact reconstructed rotator cuff structures in 29 patients, with a healing rate of 90.6% (29/32). Conclusion Arthroscopic grid-pattern dynamic rotator cuff reconstruction using autologous tendon graft is effective for IMRCT, significantly alleviating pain, improving shoulder range of motion, and restoring both functional and structural integrity, without major complication or adverse reaction.

title: Comparison of Data-Driven Phenotyping Systems for Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: Implications for Treatment Response.
abstract: Background Although emerging classification systems address the pathophysiological heterogeneity of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the implications of these subtypes for treatment responses remain unclear. We systematically evaluated three phenotyping frameworks for stratifying responses to lifestyle management. Methods This prospective observational cohort study included 618 patients with MASLD who received 48 weeks of guideline-based lifestyle management. The classification systems assessed were metabolic clusters-mild obesity/dyslipidemia-associated MASLD (MODM), age-related MASLD (AM), severe insulin resistance-associated MASLD, high lipoprotein(a)-associated MASLD (HLPAM), and severe mixed hyperlipidemia-associated MASLD (SMHLM); hepatic and cardiometabolic traits (control, liver-specific, and cardiometabolic); and biochemical patterns (hepatocellular, mixed, and cholestatic). The primary endpoints were responses in magnetic resonance imaging-derived proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) (≥30% relative liver fat reduction), alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (≥17 IU/L decrease), and liver stiffness measurements (LSM) (≥1-stage improvement in the LSM-defined fibrosis stage). Results Metabolic clusters demonstrated significantly greater temporal stability than the hepatic and cardiometabolic trait and biochemical pattern systems (62.8% vs. 56.6% vs. 53.4%, P =0.003). The HLPAM cluster demonstrated an attenuated MRI-PDFF response (odds ratio [OR], 0.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15 to 0.79), while the AM cluster showed a lower ALT response (OR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.18 to 0.62), and the MODM cluster displayed a superior LSM response compared to the others (all P <0.05). Moreover, the liver-specific cluster showed better MRI-PDFF, ALT, and LSM responses than the control cluster. However, biochemical patterns selectively stratified ALT responses, with the hepatocellular pattern demonstrating a greater response than the mixed and cholestatic patterns. Conclusion Metabolic cluster-based MASLD subtypes exhibited differential responses to lifestyle management, supporting the integration of metabolic subtyping into clinical algorithms to optimize management.

title: Three-dimensional coded aperture imaging system proposed for early breast cancer detection using low tumor-to-background ratio.
abstract: Coded aperture (CA) based image formation methods have been used in medical imaging for the past two decades. However, no commercially available Single Photon Emission Computed Tomography (SPECT) CA camera technology has been developed yet. This study investigated the lower tumor-to-background ratio (TBR) in 3D breast reconstruction with tumors. TBR is a potential factor for evaluating the malignancy of breast cancer because of its correlation with lesion size. The CA-based SPECT camera uses an iterative reconstruction algorithm called Maximum Likelihood Expectation Maximization (MLEM) with a mosaic Modified Uniformly Redundant Array (MURA) mask and anti-mask dual reconstruction. The background noise and intrinsic artifacts are suppressed by subtracting mask reconstructed images from the anti-mask images, thereby reducing the non-uniformity in the background. The reconstructed slices are then stacked to create a three-dimensional representation of the breast phantom. By employing a TBR of 5:1, mosaic MURA mask anti-mask subtraction has enhanced the quality of the reconstructed images and made it possible to detect breast lesions with a diameter of 4 mm. Furthermore, rather than using a sinogram, the proposed method can create a 3D breast phantom from a single projection. Simulation results suggest the feasibility of detecting 4 mm lesions at TBR = 5:1 using a single-projection mosaic MURA coded aperture system. Clinical validation is required to confirm translation to patient imaging.

title: Improving Radiological Quality of Proximal Femoral Nail Antirotation Fixation for Intertrochanteric Femoral Fractures: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit of Reduction Quality, Tip-Apex Distance, and Helical Blade Position.
abstract: Background The technical quality of proximal femoral nail antirotation (PFNA) fixation for intertrochanteric femoral fractures is influenced by fracture reduction and implant positioning. Reduction quality, tip-apex distance (TAD), and helical blade position are important immediate postoperative radiological indicators of fixation quality. This closed-loop clinical audit evaluated these parameters and assessed changes following targeted quality-improvement interventions. Aim To evaluate and improve the immediate postoperative radiological quality of PFNA fixation for intertrochanteric femoral fractures by comparing reduction quality, TAD, and helical blade position between baseline and re-audit cycles. Methods A retrospective baseline audit included 21 consecutive patients with intertrochanteric femoral fractures treated with PFNA between February 4, 2025, and February 3, 2026. Immediate postoperative anteroposterior (AP) and lateral radiographs were assessed for fracture reduction using predefined radiological criteria, TAD with correction for radiographic magnification, and helical blade position using the Cleveland index. Following review of the baseline findings, targeted quality-improvement interventions were implemented between April and May 2026. These included case-based discussion of reduction techniques, reinforcement of intraoperative TAD assessment, teaching on optimal blade positioning using the Cleveland index, and reinforcement of key PFNA technical principles. Following a post-intervention implementation period, 18 additional PFNA cases were assessed from June 2026 using the same eligibility criteria, radiological definitions, and outcome indicators. Between-cycle comparisons were performed using appropriate exact statistical tests for categorical variables and Welch's independent-samples t-test for mean TAD. Results At baseline, good reduction was achieved in 10/21 (47.6%) cases, TAD <25 mm in 14/21 (66.7%), and ideal blade positioning in 14/21 (66.7%), while poor reduction occurred in 4/21 (19.0%). At re-audit, good reduction increased to 12/18 (66.7%), representing an absolute increase of 19.0 percentage points, while ideal blade positioning increased to 14/18 (77.8%), an increase of 11.1 percentage points. Poor reduction decreased to 0/18 (0%). Achievement of TAD <25 mm increased modestly to 13/18 (72.2%), while mean TAD decreased from 23.6 ± 4.3 mm to 21.7 ± 3.2 mm. None of the principal between-cycle differences reached statistical significance. Conclusion Following targeted quality-improvement interventions, favorable changes were observed in fracture reduction and helical blade positioning, including elimination of poor reductions, while achievement of TAD <25 mm remained approximately 72%. Although the between-cycle differences were not statistically significant, the findings indicate encouraging quality-improvement trends and identify TAD optimization as an important target for subsequent audit cycles. Continued radiographic review, intraoperative attention to reduction and implant positioning, and periodic re-audit are recommended.

title: Reconciling Extent of Resection and Residual Tumor Volume in Glioblastoma: Sources of Discordance and a Proposed Reporting Framework.
abstract: Extent of resection (EOR) and residual tumor volume (RV) are among the few modifiable prognostic factors in glioblastoma (GBM), yet their interpretation remains complicated by substantial methodological heterogeneity. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary literature on EOR and RV as prognostic metrics in adult IDH-wild-type GBM, drawing on a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science (January 2000-March 2026), and proposes a standardized reporting framework to improve cross-study comparability. Although both metrics are consistently associated with survival, apparent disagreement between EOR- and RV-based studies largely reflects methodological rather than genuine biological discordance. Key sources of heterogeneity include inconsistent terminology (18 distinct terms identified across six decades of literature, only about half with explicit thresholds), variable postoperative MRI timing, differing segmentation methods, inconsistent definitions of contrast-enhancing versus non-enhancing tumor compartments, evolving WHO molecular classification, and inadequate adjustment for confounding by indication, tumor location, and treatment factors. The Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO)-resect classification represents an important advance toward standardization and has undergone independent revalidation, but definitional inconsistency persists more broadly. Building on these findings, this review proposes an author-derived, ten-domain reporting framework spanning study population, patient and tumor characteristics, surgical approach, imaging acquisition, segmentation methodology, EOR/RV calculation, molecular classification, confounder adjustment, statistical methods, and outcome reporting, intended to complement rather than replace existing standards such as Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) and Transparent Reporting of a Multivariable Prediction Model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis (TRIPOD). This framework has not undergone formal Delphi consensus or prospective validation and should be regarded as a preliminary proposal. Standardized, transparent reporting, potentially supported by emerging AI-based segmentation and reporting tools, may help reconcile apparently conflicting findings and strengthen future evidence synthesis regarding surgical cytoreduction in GBM.

title: When Irrigation Flows the Wrong Way: Intraoperative Regurgitation Through an Enterovesical Fistula.
abstract: Enterovesical fistulas complicate inflammatory bowel disease, particularly after restorative proctocolectomy with ileal pouch-anal anastomosis, creating pathways that may complicate endoscopic urological procedures performed under continuous irrigation. A 33-year-old man (61 kg; body mass index 18.8 kg/m²) with unclassified pancolitis (no histological features of Crohn disease in the colectomy specimen) had undergone restorative proctocolectomy with an ileal J-pouch, defunctioning loop ileostomy and ileal pouch-anal anastomosis, with repeated failed interventions for a chronic enterovesical fistula. He underwent elective laser cystolithotripsy and suprapubic catheter exchange. After induction with fentanyl, lidocaine, propofol and rocuronium, the airway was managed with a size 4 i-gel (Intersurgical Ltd, Wokingham, UK), without an orogastric tube in its gastric channel, in the lithotomy position, with gravity-fed 0.9% saline irrigation. One hour and 23 minutes after the start of surgery, clear fluid appeared at the oropharynx. The oropharynx was suctioned, the trachea was intubated, and a nasogastric tube was placed; a second episode followed two minutes later. Irrigation was stopped. The ileostomy appliance, empty at induction, was completely distended with clear fluid, and irrigation return through the cystostomy was markedly reduced. Core temperature on admission to the intermediate care unit was 33.0 °C. Ventilatory parameters, auscultation, arterial blood gas analysis, and chest radiography showed no evidence of aspiration. He was discharged on postoperative day 7. We propose that the regurgitated fluid was predominantly irrigation fluid that had migrated retrogradely through the fistula into the ileal pouch and small bowel. To our knowledge, this mechanism has not been described previously. Fistulous urinary-gastrointestinal anatomy warrants treatment as an aspiration risk factor in its own right, with gastric-channel drainage whenever a supraglottic device is used, and deliberate monitoring of irrigation input, drainage return, stomal output, and core temperature.

title: Colonic Angiosarcoma 16 Years After Pelvic Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: A Case Report.
abstract: Angiosarcomas are rare and aggressive malignant neoplasms of vascular or lymphatic endothelial origin, accounting for approximately 2% of soft-tissue sarcomas. They occur predominantly in the skin and superficial soft tissues, particularly in the head and neck region and the breast, whereas gastrointestinal involvement is exceptionally rare. Previous radiotherapy is a well-established risk factor for secondary angiosarcoma. However, radiation-associated gastrointestinal angiosarcomas are extremely uncommon and have been reported predominantly in the small bowel. We report the case of a 55-year-old woman who presented with abdominal pain, hemorrhagic ascites, intermittent rectal bleeding, severe anemia, anorexia, and weight loss 16 years after pelvic radiotherapy and cisplatin-based chemotherapy for cervical squamous cell carcinoma. Computed tomography revealed circumferential thickening of the cecum and right colon with abundant hyperdense ascites. Colonoscopy showed an obstructing, ulcerated, and contact-bleeding mass involving the cecum and right colon. Histopathological examination of endoscopic biopsies revealed a poorly differentiated malignant vascular neoplasm. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for cluster of differentiation (CD)31 and CD34 and negative for cytokeratin, CD3, CD20, and Human Herpesvirus (HHV)8, with a Ki-67 proliferation index of 40%, supporting the diagnosis of colonic angiosarcoma. Surgical resection was considered; however, the patient developed a massive bilateral pulmonary embolism and died seven days after admission. Given the prolonged latency and the histological distinction from the primary cervical carcinoma, a possible radiation-associated etiology was considered. Nevertheless, the original radiotherapy plan was unavailable, preventing definitive confirmation that the tumor arose within the irradiated field. This case highlights the diagnostic difficulty, aggressive clinical course, and poor prognosis of colonic angiosarcoma following pelvic radiotherapy.

title: Solid Pseudopapillary Neoplasm of the Pancreatic Tail With Splenic Hilar Involvement: A Case Report.
abstract: Solid pseudopapillary epithelial neoplasm (SPEN) is a rare pancreatic epithelial tumour that predominantly affects young women and is characterised by low malignant potential and favourable prognosis following complete surgical resection. A 28-year-old woman presented with intermittent left upper abdominal pain and loss of appetite for one month. Physical examination and laboratory investigations, including tumour markers, were unremarkable. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 7.4 × 7.0 × 6.4 cm well-defined cystic lesion with solid components arising from the pancreatic tail, suggestive of SPEN. The patient underwent distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy due to splenic hilar involvement. Histopathological examination and immunohistochemistry confirmed SPEN, demonstrating β-catenin and progesterone receptor positivity with a Ki-67 index <1%. SPEN is an uncommon pancreatic tumour that typically presents with non-specific symptoms, often leading to delayed diagnosis. Characteristic imaging findings combined with histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation are essential for accurate diagnosis. Complete surgical resection remains the treatment of choice and is associated with favourable outcomes. SPEN should be considered in young women presenting with pancreatic cystic lesions and vague abdominal symptoms. Complete surgical excision by distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy can achieve excellent oncological outcomes, even in cases with splenic hilar involvement.

title: Blood Management Strategies in Placenta Accreta Spectrum.
abstract: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) presents a major challenge in obstetric care because attempted placental separation may result in rapid and life-threatening hemorrhage. As PAS is often suspected before delivery, there is an opportunity to identify correctable risks and prepare for anticipated blood loss. This narrative review examines blood-management strategies throughout the antenatal, intraoperative, and postoperative periods. A targeted narrative search of PubMed and PubMed Central, supplemented by searches of journal and publisher websites, was conducted for literature available through September 2026. Antenatal management focuses on identifying and treating maternal anemia, referring patients to experienced centers, and developing a multidisciplinary delivery plan. Perioperative preparation includes coordination with the transfusion service, timely access to appropriate blood components, clear criteria for activating a major obstetric hemorrhage protocol, and defined responsibilities for each team member. Blood-product preparation should be individualized according to the severity suggested by prenatal imaging and the anticipated anatomical extent of placental invasion, ranging from suspected accreta to increta or percreta. Key intraoperative blood-conservation measures include intraoperative cell salvage and timely administration of tranexamic acid when clinically indicated, particularly during significant hemorrhage. Viscoelastic hemostatic testing, fibrinogen-directed therapy, and selected interventional radiology procedures may also contribute to individualized management. However, evidence supporting these interventions remains inconsistent and is frequently derived from observational studies, expert consensus, or broader obstetric hemorrhage populations rather than PAS-specific randomized trials. Consequently, blood-management plans should reflect the anticipated severity of PAS, the patient's clinical condition, and the expertise and resources available at the treating institution. A structured and individualized approach linking antenatal optimization, multidisciplinary preparation, timely hemorrhage control, and postoperative surveillance may support safer and more efficient care for patients with PAS.

title: When Hypercapnia Misleads: A Case of Respiratory-Onset Motor Neuron Disease.
abstract: Motor neuron disease (MND) most commonly presents with limb or bulbar weakness; however, a minority of patients present with respiratory-onset disease, posing significant diagnostic challenges. We report the case of a 78-year-old woman with a background of small airways disease and rheumatoid arthritis not requiring treatment for many years, who presented with a two-year history of progressive exertional dyspnoea, unintentional weight loss, and functional decline. Before diagnosis, she underwent extensive investigation across primary and secondary care, including chest radiography, spirometry, computed tomography imaging, and ear, nose, and throat specialist assessment, without a unifying diagnosis being established. On admission, venous blood gas demonstrated compensated hypercapnia, which was attributed to obstructive airways disease. She subsequently developed hypercapnic respiratory failure, and a clinical diagnosis of MND was made on the basis of generalised muscle wasting, fasciculations, brisk lower-limb reflexes, and electromyography findings. Non-invasive ventilation was initiated with significant clinical improvement. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of respiratory-onset MND, the risk of anchoring bias in the interpretation of biochemical markers, and the importance of considering neuromuscular causes when respiratory symptoms are disproportionate to radiological and biochemical findings.

title: Solitary Rectal Ulcer Syndrome Mimicking Ulcerative Colitis: A Case Report.
abstract: Solitary rectal ulcer syndrome (SRUS) is a benign rectal disorder associated with abnormal defecation and mucosal prolapse. Its clinical and endoscopic features may mimic inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). We report the case of a 28-year-old woman with longstanding obstructed defecation who presented with recurrent bloody mucus discharge and severe iron-deficiency anemia (hemoglobin 6.6 g/dL), which was treated with intravenous iron infusions. C-reactive protein was normal, whereas fecal calprotectin was markedly elevated. Initial colonoscopy showed erythematous and congested mucosa extending from the anal verge to 20 cm, with a large ulcer, raising suspicion of ulcerative colitis. However, the initial biopsies were inconclusive. Following clinical worsening, repeat colonoscopy revealed a 5-cm elevated rectal lesion with central ulceration. Histological examination demonstrated epithelial loss, granulation tissue, villiform crypt changes, and characteristic fibromuscular hyperplasia of the lamina propria, establishing the diagnosis of SRUS. Magnetic resonance defecography revealed an anterior rectocele and internal rectal prolapse, while anorectal manometry demonstrated dyssynergic defecation. Conservative measures and biofeedback provided incomplete improvement, with persistent rectal bleeding. Given the documented internal rectal prolapse and refractory symptoms, laparoscopic ventral rectopexy was performed, resulting in a favorable postoperative clinical course with marked symptomatic improvement and normalization of hemoglobin to 13.7 g/dL. SRUS should be considered when inflammatory-appearing rectal lesions are not supported by histological evidence of IBD, particularly in patients with obstructed defecation.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Automated Analysis and Interpretation of Intravascular Ultrasound in Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) leads to considerable morbidity and mortality worldwide. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) is an imaging modality to guide percutaneous coronary intervention; however, it requires time-consuming, expert-dependent manual analysis. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly used for IVUS analysis, but there is limited evidence on its diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility. This review aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance and clinical usefulness of AI for automated IVUS analysis of coronary arteries. The research protocol was prospectively registered (PROSPERO, CRD420261454806) and followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines for systematic reviews. PubMed/MEDLINE and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception through July 23, 2026, and July 26, 2026, respectively, for publications assessing AI, machine learning, or deep learning algorithms for the automated analysis of coronary IVUS, including segmentation of structures, identification of plaque types, and quantitative measurements. Two reviewers independently screened and selected eligible studies and extracted the data. The risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 (Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) and visualized using robvis, and the GRADE approach was used to rate the certainty of evidence. Of the 802 records identified (PubMed, n = 216; Cochrane CENTRAL, n = 586), eight studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in this review. They reported on the performance of convolutional neural networks, U-Net/U-Net++, Efficient-UNet, DeepLabv3+-based models, and gradient boosting in segmenting lumen, vessel, plaque, and stent in coronary IVUS. The Dice similarity coefficient ranged from 0.67 to 0.97, and the intersection over union for segmentation (including Jaccard similarity) ranged from 0.66 to 0.97, with the best performance for lumen and vessel segmentation and the poorest for stent and calcium. The sensitivity and specificity ranged from 62% to 90% and 88% to 99%, respectively, with the correlation to expert assessment generally above 0.9. Overall, the risk of bias was mainly related to patient selection (five out of eight studies) and the reference standard (three out of eight studies), and none of the studies was rated as having a high risk of bias. Due to between-study heterogeneity in the tasks, reference standards, and outcome measures, a meta-analysis was not performed, and the certainty of evidence was rated as low. The current evidence suggests that AI-based methods have good potential for analyzing coronary IVUS with acceptable accuracy, which could be helpful for high-throughput IVUS interpretation in clinical practice. They appear to perform best at segmenting lumen and vessel structures and worst at segmenting stent and calcium. However, due to the overall low certainty of evidence from these mostly retrospective studies, their use should be limited to complementing the work of experts in cardiovascular medicine.

title: Endoscopic Excision of a C5 Osteoid Osteoma With Intraoperative Computed Tomography.
abstract: Osteoid osteoma is a benign bone tumor characterized by nocturnal pain, with a predilection for teenage male patients. A 15-year-old boy presented with a two-month history of neck pain and was referred to our hospital, where imaging studies revealed an osteoid osteoma of the cervical vertebra. As he was preparing for a national basketball tournament and wished to return to sports as soon as possible, minimally invasive surgery was performed to excise the tumor using an endoscopic technique with intraoperative computed tomography, which confirmed that the extent of excision matched the preoperative surgical plan. His pain improved immediately postoperatively, and he was able to return to sports three months after surgery. At two years postoperatively, follow-up imaging showed no recurrence, progressive spinal malalignment, or spondylolisthesis.

title: Mandibular Canal Morphometry and Anatomical Variations Using Cone-Beam Computed Tomography in a North Indian Population: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Introduction The present study aimed to evaluate the morphology, dimensions, anatomical variations, and spatial characteristics of the mandibular canal (MC) in a North Indian population using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). The associations between MC characteristics and sex, age, and laterality were also assessed to identify clinically relevant patterns of anatomical variation. Materials and methods This retrospective database observational study was conducted using 400 CBCT scans of adults aged ≥18 years between June 2024 and May 2025. The scans were evaluated using multiplanar and curved planar reconstructions. MC course, length, vertical and horizontal diameters, buccolingual position, anterior loop, bifid and trifid canals, and accessory mental foramina were assessed. Two calibrated observers independently evaluated the scans, with repeated assessments performed to establish measurement reliability. Differences according to sex and side, as well as associations with age, were analyzed using generalized estimating equations (GEE) to account for bilateral observations. Multinomial logistic GEE were used for categorical canal patterns. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results Among the 400 participants, 220 were males and 180 were females, with a mean age of 42.6 ± 12.1 years. Males demonstrated significantly greater canal length, vertical diameter, horizontal diameter, and anterior loop length than females. Bifid canals were significantly more common in males than in females. The ascending canal morphology was the most common pattern, followed by catenary and straight configurations, with no significant sex differences. No significant right-left differences were observed in canal dimensions or anatomical variants. The canal was predominantly centrally positioned buccolingually across all tooth regions, ranging from 67.5% in the second premolar region to 76.0% in the third molar region. Increasing age was significantly associated with reduced canal length, whereas other measured characteristics showed no significant age-related associations. Conclusion MC anatomy demonstrates substantial morphological variability, with significant differences related to sex and age but limited bilateral asymmetry. CBCT assessment provides a detailed characterization of canal dimensions, course, and anatomical variants. Recognition of these variations is important for individualized preoperative evaluation and for minimizing neurovascular complications during mandibular surgical procedures.

title: Bilateral Adrenal Masses, Extreme Catecholamine Excess, and Hypercalcitoninemia With Metastatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasia: A Diagnostic Dilemma.
abstract: A 40-year-old man presented with back pain, urinary retention, mild unilateral weakness, weight loss, hypercalcemia, and newly recognized hypertension. During the early admission, blood pressure became markedly labile, reaching 225/106 mmHg. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated approximately 10-cm bilateral heterogeneous adrenal masses and diffuse lytic skeletal metastases. Biochemical testing showed profound catecholamine excess, including urine metanephrine/creatinine 42,040 µg/g creatinine (reference range: 29-158 µg/g), normetanephrine/creatinine 6,079 µg/g creatinine (reference range: 53-659 µg/g), and vanillylmandelic acid/creatinine 212 mg/g creatinine (reference range: 1.1-4.1 mg/g). Serum calcitonin was 4,680 pg/mL (reference ≤8.4), with carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) 239 ng/mL (reference <3.8 ng/mL for a non-smoker). Expert review of a bone biopsy showed a metastatic well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor, WHO grade 3 (2017), with Ki-67 approximately 40%. The tumor expressed chromogranin, synaptophysin, pancytokeratin, thyroid transcription factor 1 (TTF-1), CEA, paired box 8 (PAX8), and cytokeratin (CK) 7 but was negative for calcitonin, thyroglobulin, CK20, GATA3, and S100. Small polypoid lesions at the tip of the tongue, considered possible mucosal neuromas, together with thyroid calcifications raised concern for multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2B; however, thyroid fine-needle aspiration, RET testing, and functional imaging were not completed before rapid clinical deterioration. The patient received alpha-blockade, palliative spinal radiotherapy, and carboplatin/etoposide; his course was complicated by profound pancytopenia, extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli bacteremia, respiratory and renal failure, gastrointestinal bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, and death. The case illustrates clinicopathologic discordance: the biochemical phenotype strongly favored pheochromocytoma, whereas metastatic-site histology did not establish the primary site.

title: A Brain Metastasis in Search of Its Origin: Occult Primary Non-small Cell Lung Cancer.
abstract: We present a case of a 67-year-old man who presented with right-sided hemiparesis and headache and was found to have a solitary left temporoparietal cerebral lesion on MRI, initially favoring a primary brain tumor. Further workup was unremarkable and the patient underwent surgical resection of the cerebral lesion. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry favored a metastatic pulmonary adenocarcinoma, though imaging scans showed no primary lung lesion. Subsequent PET-CT demonstrated hypermetabolic mediastinal, hilar, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, consistent with occult primary non-small cell lung cancer. The patient underwent stereotactic gamma knife radiotherapy to the resection bed, followed by systemic chemotherapy with cisplatin and vinorelbine. At the time of writing, two of three planned chemotherapy cycles had been completed, with radiological response assessment scheduled after completion of the treatment. This case adds to the limited literature on occult primary non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and supports early tissue diagnosis as key to appropriate management.

Histopathology and immunohistochemistry favored a metastatic pulmonary adenocarcinoma, though imaging scans showed no primary lung lesion. Subsequent PET-CT demonstrated hypermetabolic mediastinal, hilar, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, consistent with occult primary non-small cell lung cancer. The patient underwent stereotactic gamma knife radiotherapy to the resection bed, followed by systemic chemotherapy with cisplatin and vinorelbine. At the time of writing, two of three planned chemotherapy cycles had been completed, with radiological response assessment scheduled after completion of the treatment. title: Lower Back Pain As the Initial Manifestation of Primary Follicular B-cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma of the Bone Marrow: A Case Report.
abstract: Follicular B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (B-NHL) is a malignant disease of the lymphatic system that primarily affects the lymph nodes. The primary presentation of follicular B-NHL in the bone is extremely rare. The patient, a 53-year-old woman, developed non-radiating lower back pain at the age of 52. Diagnostic evaluation via magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) revealed a solid intraosseous mass in the L3 vertebral body, an L2 compression fracture, and extensive metastatic disease involving the ribs, vertebral bodies, ilium, and cranial vault. Three months after the onset of lower back pain, a CT-guided biopsy of the ilium confirmed the presence of follicular B-NHL lymphoma cells. These cells tested positive for CD10, BCL6, and BCL2, as well as for the minimal residual disease marker t(14;18). Cranial MRI showed osseous lesions in the cranial vault but no intra-axial lesions. No extraosseous metastases were detected. Risk stratification indicated stage IVA, Follicular Lymphoma International Prognostic Index (FLIPI): 4-5, and FLIPI2: 3. Six cycles (one per month) of therapy with rituximab, bendamustine, and intravenous immunoglobulins proved ineffective after five months. Twelve months after symptom onset, the lymphoma progressed and transformed into diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Various attempts to treat the DLBCL were also unsuccessful. Twenty months after the onset of lower back pain, the patient died of sepsis. In summary, this case demonstrates that follicular B-NHL can initially involve only the bones and manifest solely as lumbar back pain. In summary, this case demonstrates that follicular B-NHL can initially involve only the bones and manifest solely as lumbar back pain. Despite chemotherapy, symptoms may worsen, and B-NHL may transform into fatal DLBCL.

title: Extranodal Marginal Zone Lymphoma of the Floor of the Mouth: A Rare Entity With Management Challenges.
abstract: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma) involving the oral cavity is rare, and localization to the floor of the mouth is particularly uncommon. Its indolent course and nonspecific clinical presentation may lead to diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Diagnosis relies on histopathological examination combined with immunohistochemical analysis to establish the B-cell phenotype and exclude other small B-cell lymphomas. We report the case of a 48-year-old man with stage IIE MALT lymphoma of the floor of the mouth associated with ipsilateral submandibular lymph node involvement. Given the large tumor volume, systemic therapy was initially favored. The patient received four cycles of rituximab monotherapy with an insufficient response. A repeat biopsy excluded histological transformation, and rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisolone chemoimmunotherapy was subsequently administered, with persistent local disease. External radiotherapy was then delivered to the oral cavity and cervical lymph node regions (24 Gy), with a boost to the floor-of-mouth lesion to a total dose of 30 Gy. Follow-up positron emission tomography/computed tomography demonstrated a complete metabolic response, and the patient remained clinically free of recurrence 18 months after radiotherapy. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of MALT lymphoma at an exceptional oral site and illustrates the importance of radiotherapy in achieving local disease control after an insufficient response to systemic therapy.

title: Intraoperative and Implant-Related Parameters of Isolated Intertrochanteric Rotational Osteotomy for Pathological Femoral Torsion: A Descriptive Single-Center Report.
abstract: Background Isolated intertrochanteric rotational osteotomy (ITO) corrects pathological femoral torsion at the intertrochanteric level through a planar osteotomy stabilized with a fixed-angle plate. Functional results of joint-preserving femoral osteotomies appear regularly, yet the parameters that define how the operation is actually performed, including the rotational correction angle, the implant configuration, operative time, and length of hospital stay, are rarely quantified. This report documents these intraoperative and implant-related parameters in a procedurally homogeneous single-technique cohort. Methods Patients treated with isolated rotational or derotational ITO between 2002 and 2009 at one tertiary center were reviewed retrospectively. The descriptive variables fixed in advance were the intraoperative rotational correction angle, the implant configuration (plate angle, plate length, plate offset, and number of fixation screws), skin-to-skin operative time, and length of hospital stay. No inferential or outcome analysis was undertaken. Variables are summarized as mean ± standard deviation or as counts and percentages. Results Sixty patients were analyzed (42 women, 18 men; mean age 28 ± 13 years). A rotational osteotomy was carried out in 43 patients (71.7%), and a derotational osteotomy in 17 (28.3%); the operated side was left in 28 (46.7%) and right in 32 (53.3%). The mean rotational correction angle was 18 ± 9°. Fixation used a fixed-angle plate with a mean plate angle of 113 ± 11° and a mean length of 67 ± 10 mm, secured with a mean of 4 ± 1 screws. Plate offset was 10 mm in 35 patients (58.3%), absent in 16 (26.7%), 5 mm in five patients (8.3%), and 15 mm in four patients (6.7%). The mean skin-to-skin operative time was 124 ± 27 minutes, and the mean length of hospital stay was 12 ± 2 days. Conclusions This report quantifies the intraoperative and implant-related profile of isolated ITO in a single-technique cohort. The intraoperative correction angle averaged 18° (median 15°), an intraoperatively set correction rather than one referenced to a measured preoperative torsion, with wide individual variation; fixation followed a single fixed-angle principle using blade and angle plates of comparable geometry. Because preoperative torsion was not quantified radiographically in this cohort, the correction angle is reported as an intraoperatively set surgical parameter. These figures are descriptive and document how the procedure was executed at one center during this period; they are not outcome, survivorship, or safety measures.

title: Explantation, Guided Bone Regeneration, and Digitally Planned Implant Replacement in Advanced Peri-Implantitis: A Case Report With 12-Month Follow-Up.
abstract: When advanced peri-implantitis affects several implants, it is necessary to decide which implants to retain and which to remove before planning any reconstruction. This case highlights the indications for explantation in advanced peri-implantitis, the role of guided bone regeneration in reconstructing compromised sites, and the benefits of digitally planned placement of new implants. The 12-month follow-up underscores the clinical relevance of sustained peri-implant health. We present the clinical case of a 65-year-old man with arterial hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus under treatment (glycated hemoglobin 6% at baseline, non-smoker) who presented with a fracture of his upper fixed prosthesis and esthetic concerns. Generalized stage IV grade B periodontitis was diagnosed, along with peri-implantitis in the seven existing implants, whose defects were classified on cone beam computed tomography between classes Ib and IIIc. Six implants were assigned a hopeless prognosis, and one was given a guarded prognosis. After initial periodontal and prosthetic therapy, six implants were removed, with forceps in the maxilla and with a trephine followed by forceps in the mandible, and the root remnants were extracted. The retained implant was treated by implantoplasty and surface decontamination. The explantation sites were regenerated with allograft and a resorbable collagen membrane. Four months later, 12 implants were placed with static guided surgery, using a mucosa-supported guide in the maxilla and two bone-supported guides for trimming and placement in the mandible, all achieving an insertion torque above 35 N·cm. At position 44, plasma rich in growth factors mixed with autologous bone was added. Rehabilitation was completed with screw-retained fixed prostheses in both arches. At 12 months after delivery of the definitive prostheses, the probing depth remained between 3 and 4 mm in all the implants, with no bleeding on probing and no evident radiographic progression of marginal bone loss compared to the initial record. This case demonstrates that a stepwise sequence of selective explantation, regeneration, and guided placement of new implants is feasible in advanced peri-implantitis; however, as a single observation in a well-controlled, non-smoking patient, it demonstrates short-term clinical feasibility only and cannot establish effectiveness, predictability, or reproducibility.

title: A Volumetric Anatomy-Aware, Prompt-Guided Adaptation Framework for the Segment Anything Model in Head and Neck Radiotherapy.
abstract: Background Head and neck (H&N) radiotherapy planning requires accurate segmentation of numerous organs at risk (OARs), yet many critical structures, such as the optic nerves, chiasm, and cochleae, are small, poorly contrasted on CT, and prone to high inter-observer variability in manual contouring. Recent foundation models like Segment Anything Model (SAM) and its 3D medical variants (SAM-Med3D) offer prompt-based, interactive segmentation, but their real-world utility for H&N small OARs is hindered by unreliable prompt sources and unstable performance on fine anatomical targets. To address these issues, this work proposes an anatomy-aware prompt generation and prompt-guided adaptation tailored specifically for small-structure segmentation to improve both precision and automation feasibility. Purpose To address these challenges, we developed a domain-adapted framework, SAM-FT-HN, by fine-tuning a volumetric SAM backbone (SAM-Med3D) for automated delineation of H&N OARs in radiotherapy planning. Our approach incorporates a coarse-to-fine pipeline in which a lightweight localization network automatically generates organ-specific prompts and candidate regions, followed by a fine-tuned volumetric SAM backbone for refinement. We further introduced task-specific strategies including region-of-interest (ROI)-guided tiny-organ enhancement and organ-specific threshold calibration to improve performance on small structures. The primary objective is to develop and evaluate a fully automated, anatomy-aware adaptation of SAM-Med3D for H&N OAR segmentation, with a secondary objective of improving small-organ segmentation. We systematically compared SAM-FT-HN against baseline SAM-Med3D and nnUNet models quantitatively and qualitatively. Methods We used an institutional H&N CT dataset of 211 patients with manual delineations of 23 OARs, standardized for training, validation, and testing. Eighty percent of cases were used for training and validation, and twenty percent for testing. The testing phase used CT volumes only, and ground-truth masks were used solely for metric calculation. A coarse localization network was trained to generate automatic prompts and ROI candidates. SAM-FT-HN was fine-tuned using task-specific adaptations, and small-organ refinement was performed using ROI-guided enhancement and organ-specific threshold calibration. nnUNet was trained using its automated configuration pipeline. Performance was evaluated using overlap and boundary metrics. Results For large OARs, SAM-FT-HN achieved a mean Dice of 0.814 compared with 0.791 for nnUNet and substantially higher than SAM-Med3D (0.609). For small organs, SAM-FT-HN improved the mean Dice from 0.300 to 0.669 compared with SAM-Med3D and reduced HD95 by approximately 65%, although nnUNet remained higher in average small-organ Dice (0.720). Overall, across all organs, SAM-FT-HN achieved a mean Dice score of 0.770, compared with 0.769 for nnUNet. Overall, SAM-FT-HN showed no statistically significant difference from nnUNet in the patient-level analysis, while substantially outperforming the original SAM-Med3D baseline. Conclusion Fine-tuning a foundation model with anatomy-aware automatic prompting, coarse-to-fine localization, and adaptive thresholding markedly improves small-organ segmentation, substantially mitigating a key limitation of the original foundation model. SAM-FT-HN offers a competitive approach for H&N radiotherapy contouring, with potential for future adaptive workflows.

title: Epidermoid Cyst of the Cecum: A Case Report of an Exceptionally Rare Entity and Review of the Literature.
abstract: Epidermoid cysts of the cecum are extremely rare benign lesions of the gastrointestinal tract. Their diagnosis remains challenging due to the lack of specific clinical symptoms and inconclusive radiological findings. Consequently, accurate preoperative diagnosis is difficult, with lesions often being misdiagnosed as appendiceal mucoceles, gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs), duplication cysts, or adnexal masses. We report the case of a 59-year-old male who presented with right lower quadrant abdominal pain and a palpable mass. Comprehensive diagnostic imaging, including abdominal ultrasonography, abdominopelvic computed tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), revealed a well-circumscribed cystic lesion arising from the cecal wall, initially concerning for a cecal neoplasm or appendiceal mucocele. The patient underwent a successful right hemicolectomy, and histopathological examination definitively confirmed a cecal epidermoid cyst lined by stratified squamous epithelium containing keratinaceous debris. Postoperative recovery was uneventful. Although exceptionally rare, epidermoid cysts should be included in the differential diagnosis of right lower quadrant masses. Despite the limited number of reported cases, complete surgical excision remains the definitive treatment of choice, providing an excellent long-term prognosis with no evidence of recurrence.

title: Multilevel Lumbar Epidural Angiolipoma: A Case Report.
abstract: Spinal angiolipomas are rare benign tumors composed of mature adipose tissue and vascular elements, most commonly located in the thoracic epidural space. Lumbar involvement is considerably less frequent, and variable proportions of adipose and vascular tissue may result in atypical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics and diagnostic uncertainty. We report the case of a 36-year-old woman with an approximately one-year history of persistent low back pain associated with subjective bilateral lower-extremity weakness despite a preserved neurological examination. An initial non-contrast lumbar MRI was interpreted as showing no significant abnormality other than minimal degenerative changes; however, retrospective review revealed a subtle posterior epidural lesion. Because of persistent symptoms, further investigation with contrast-enhanced MRI was performed, demonstrating an elongated epidural lesion extending from L1 to L3, predominantly involving the posterior and right posterolateral epidural space with associated foraminal extension. The lesion demonstrated areas of low T1 signal intensity and intense homogeneous contrast enhancement. The patient underwent L1-L3 laminoplasty and gross-total resection. Intraoperatively, the lesion had a macroscopically adipose appearance and was moderately vascular. Histopathological examination demonstrated mature adipose tissue admixed with numerous vascular channels, confirming the diagnosis of spinal angiolipoma. Postoperatively, pain and subjective lower-extremity weakness improved without new neurological deficits, and early postoperative MRI showed no evidence of residual or recurrent tumor. This case highlights the variable imaging appearance of lumbar spinal angiolipomas and the value of correlating MRI characteristics with intraoperative and histopathological findings, particularly in enhancing epidural lesions without a predominantly fatty appearance.

title: Fever and Painful Skin Lesions: When to Consider Sweet's Syndrome.
abstract: Sweet's syndrome is an acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis characterised by fever, neutrophilia, and painful cutaneous lesions. We describe a case of a 31-year-old male admitted with a two-week history of fever up to 39°C and painful erythematous papules, scattered and coalescing into plaques over the trunk and limbs, together with pustules on an erythematous base over the palms and dorsum of the hands. No relevant epidemiological exposure or recent drug exposure was identified. Investigation showed an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 40 mm/h, leucocytosis of 14,380/µL with 77% neutrophils and no eosinophilia, and a C-reactive protein of 1.21 mg/dL. Liver and renal function, albumin, lactate dehydrogenase, serum iron, ferritin, and serum protein electrophoresis were normal, and a respiratory viral panel was negative. Blood, urine, and pustule cultures, an interferon-gamma release assay, and serology for human immunodeficiency virus, syphilis, hepatitis A, B, C, and E viruses, cytomegalovirus, and Epstein-Barr virus were negative, as was an autoantibody panel. Serum immunoglobulin A was below the detection limit (<0.07 g/L) before corticosteroid therapy and on all repeat measurements, including after treatment had been discontinued, with normal immunoglobulin G and M, and IgG-based coeliac serology was negative. Computed tomography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis and peripheral blood immunophenotyping showed no abnormalities. A skin biopsy demonstrated intraepidermal blisters and a superficial perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate without vasculitis, spongiform pustules, or psoriasiform changes. The clinical and laboratory criteria for classical Sweet's syndrome were fulfilled, and the histology was compatible with, although not classical for, the syndrome. Prednisolone 60 mg/day (approximately 0.6 mg/kg/day) was started on clinical suspicion of the syndrome. After one week, the fever had resolved, but the lesions worsened slightly, prompting escalation to 100 mg/day (approximately 1 mg/kg/day), after which they regressed progressively and resolved completely within three weeks of dose escalation, with normalisation of the leucocyte count. Corticosteroids were tapered and discontinued before the three-month assessment, at which there was no relapse and no evidence of malignancy. This case illustrates three practical points: an acral pustular morphology does not exclude the diagnosis; early worsening under corticosteroid therapy may reflect an initial dose insufficient for body weight rather than an incorrect diagnosis, once infection has been rigorously excluded; and the coexisting finding of selective immunoglobulin A deficiency carries independent implications for coeliac disease screening and long-term follow-up.

title: Managing Severe Proximal Femoral Fibrous Dysplasia in a Young Adult Using Hemiarthroplasty in a Resource-Constrained Healthcare System: A Case Report.
abstract: Fibrous dysplasia of the proximal femur may lead to progressive deformity, pain, and pathological fractures, with shepherd's crook deformity representing one of its most severe manifestations. Although valgus osteotomy with intramedullary fixation is considered the preferred surgical treatment, extensive bone destruction and limited healthcare resources may preclude conventional reconstruction. We present a case of severe proximal femoral fibrous dysplasia successfully managed with bipolar cemented hemiarthroplasty in a resource-constrained healthcare setting. A 25-year-old man presented with progressive left hip pain, severe proximal femoral deformity, and impaired ambulation. Radiographic evaluation demonstrated lateral bowing of the proximal femur, while histopathological examination following core biopsy confirmed fibrous dysplasia. Internal fixation using an intramedullary nail was initially planned; however, intraoperative findings revealed extensive fibro-osseous replacement, severely compromised bone quality, and inadequate cortical support, making stable fixation technically impossible. Because more complex reconstructive procedures were not covered by the national health insurance system, a bipolar cemented hemiarthroplasty, augmented with plate fixation of the osteotomized fragments, was performed as a salvage procedure. The postoperative course was uneventful, with marked pain relief, improved gait, and satisfactory functional recovery at 10 months of follow-up (Oxford Hip Score 34/48). Conventional fixation for shepherd's crook deformity requires adequate residual cortical bone to achieve stable implant fixation. In cases with extensive cortical destruction and bone stock too thin to support reliable press-fit fixation, cemented hemiarthroplasty may represent a practical alternative. Preservation of the native acetabulum may also reduce postoperative instability while providing satisfactory functional outcomes. Bipolar cemented hemiarthroplasty may be an effective salvage option for selected patients with severe proximal femoral fibrous dysplasia when conventional fixation is technically unfeasible, particularly in resource-constrained healthcare systems.

title: Phyllodes Tumors of the Breast in 2026: A Contemporary Narrative Review of Diagnosis, Surgical Margins, Prognosis, and Emerging Therapies.
abstract: Phyllodes tumors of the breast are rare fibroepithelial neoplasms characterized by significant heterogeneity regarding morphology, biological behavior, and clinical outcome. This review summarizes current developments in the diagnosis, histopathological and molecular classification, therapeutic management, and emerging technologies associated with phyllodes tumors of the breast. A literature search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, and Google Scholar, focusing on publications from the 2000-2026 period. The literature search covered publications from January 1, 2000, to September 30, 2026, and was last updated on September 30, 2026. Mammography, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance imaging contribute to preoperative assessment, although significant diagnostic overlap with fibroadenomas persists. Core needle biopsy is a key diagnostic tool, yet lesion heterogeneity can limit the accuracy of histological classification. Advances in molecular pathology have identified mutations and pathways associated with the progression and aggressiveness of phyllodes tumors, though these have not yet replaced morphological assessment. Surgical excision with negative margins remains the primary therapeutic approach, while the risk of local recurrence depends on histological grade, surgical margins, and other clinicopathological characteristics. Radiotherapy in phyllodes tumors of the breast appears to offer benefits primarily regarding local control in selected high-risk cases. Emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, radiomics, and digital pathology, are proving to be promising tools for diagnosis, grading, and prognostic assessment. Overall, modern management of phyllodes tumors of the breast is shifting toward more personalized and multifactorial approaches.
